methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort study of 308 HER2-positive breast cancer patients with well-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria. Primary endpoint (pCR) and secondary endpoint (DFS) are clearly defined per standard criteria. Multivariate logistic regression for pCR and Cox regression for DFS are appropriately employed. Key limitation is the very unbalanced group sizes (252 HER2 3+ vs. 56 HER2 2+/FISH+), which substantially reduces statistical power for subgroup analyses in the HER2 2+/FISH+ group. No correction for multiple comparisons in the extensive subgroup analyses. Study start date is redacted, limiting full assessment of treatment-era consistency.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study addresses a clinically important and evolving question: whether the HER2 2+/FISH+ subgroup derives comparable benefit from dual-target NAT as the HER2 3+ subgroup. The finding that dual-target therapy does not significantly improve pCR in HER2 2+/FISH+ patients is hypothesis-generating and relevant to ongoing debates about precision HER2 therapy. The interaction with HR status adds clinical nuance. However, this is single-center with 49-month median follow-up and no OS data.

reporting_quality.justification: Patient selection, baseline characteristics, outcome definitions, and statistical methods are adequately reported per STROBE standards. Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank tests and multivariate Cox regression results are provided. However, the study start date is redacted, treatment-era heterogeneity is not addressed, adverse event data are absent (acknowledged by authors), and no data are publicly shared. Some text duplication in the abstract and methods (sentences repeated verbatim) suggests incomplete editing.

novelty_literature.justification: While the broad question of HER2 IHC 3+ vs. 2+/FISH+ in NAT is not entirely novel and has been addressed in prior studies (e.g., Atallah et al. 2023, Chiu et al. 2023), this study adds value by explicitly examining the interaction between HER2 IHC level and HR status for both pCR and DFS in a Chinese population. The finding that dual-target benefit from pertuzumab is restricted to HER2 3+/HR-negative patients and absent in HER2 2+/FISH+ patients is an important observation, though confirmatory rather than first-in-class.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable with appropriate logical structure and tables for the main comparisons. However, there is notable text duplication (sentences repeated in the abstract and discussion), the study start date is redacted in methods, and the Cox regression section conflates some p-values. The discussion is thorough but contains some speculative mechanistic claims presented with insufficient hedging. The final paragraph of the abstract is duplicated. Overall presentation is adequate but requires editorial attention.

key_strengths: Clinically relevant question about differential benefit of dual HER2 blockade by IHC level, with particular focus on the HR status interaction
Large Chinese NAT cohort (n=308) with 49-month median follow-up providing DFS data beyond pCR
Multivariate analyses for both pCR (logistic) and DFS (Cox) with appropriate covariates
Clinically actionable finding: pertuzumab benefit concentrated in HER2 3+/HR-negative subgroup
key_concerns: Severely unbalanced group sizes (56 vs. 252) make HER2 2+/FISH+ subgroup analyses underpowered and unstable; acknowledged but not quantified
Multiple subgroup comparisons without correction for multiplicity inflates false-positive risk across the many pCR comparisons
Study start date redacted; treatment-era heterogeneity spanning 2017-2020 (mix of pertuzumab availability) not addressed
No adverse event analysis despite this being an important component of the dual-target therapy risk-benefit assessment
Text duplication and inconsistent p-value reporting suggest manuscript was submitted without complete editorial review
chief_reviewer.rationale: A clinically relevant single-center study with adequate follow-up and appropriate multivariable analyses, but substantially limited by small HER2 2+/FISH+ group size, absence of adverse event data, and manuscript quality issues; major revisions are needed to address statistical power limitations and editorial problems before acceptance at a tier-3 journal.
